subject: MedSecure: vendor roster validation & evidence package
body:
From: Priyanka Rao <security@medsecure.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSecure Compliance Team <compliance@medsecure.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor roster + evidence request (CAIQ / SIG)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the quick intro over the phone earlier. As part of our procurement security review for MedSecure Health, we need a concise vendor roster and evidence package covering the following items by 2025-09-12: 

- Authoritative subprocessor list (name, service, location, purpose, contract start date)
- SOC 2 / ISO attestations (PDFs or links) or statement if not available
- CAIQ answers for infrastructure and data protection (or SIG-lite responses)
- SBOM or runtime dependency list for the inference runtime (high level is fine)
- Confirmation of KMS/HSM usage and key separation model (who can decrypt)

Preferred format: CSV for roster + single ZIP with artifacts or a shared Drive link. Let us know if you need to redact any vendor cost/pricing. Also confirm whether scope should be global or EU-only (we're primarily concerned about data residency and subprocessors processing EU data).

Appreciate it — we can review and give feedback in 48 hours once received.

Best,
Priyanka Rao
Senior InfoSec Manager
MedSecure Health
security@medsecure.com

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <security@medsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + evidence request (CAIQ / SIG)

Hi Priyanka — thanks for the note and the timeline. We'll assemble a package and aim to deliver preliminary materials by EOD 2025-09-08, with the full set by 2025-09-12 if needed. A few quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly: 

- Scope: Do you want the roster for all Redwood production services or only those that touch EU customer data? (We can filter by data-scoped subprocessors.)
- SBOM: is a high-level component list sufficient (libraries/kernels/containers) or do you require signed SBOM artifacts?
- SIG vs CAIQ: if SIG-lite is acceptable we'll provide the condensed answers to speed review.

Action plan: I'll coordinate with Security and Platform to produce:
1) CSV roster (name, service, geo, role, contract start)
2) Links to public attestations + copies where available
3) SBOM high-level PDF and notes on runtime image builds
4) Short write-up on KMS/HSM model and separation controls

Marissa: can you confirm if procurement wants any additional redlines captured?
Karthik/Alex: can you start a quick inventory for subprocessors that process EU data specifically?

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor roster + evidence request (CAIQ / SIG)

Mina / team — putting some technical notes here for the final package: 

- Subprocessors: I'll pull the authoritative list from our contract DB and filter by data plane vs telemetry. We should mark which vendors store encrypted customer data vs transient compute.
- Redaction: remove cost fields and any internal account IDs before sharing externally. Leave vendor legal names and service descriptions.
- SBOM: we can supply a signed SPDx top-level SBOM for the runtime layer; for kernels and closed-source drivers we will provide an inventory of binary dependencies and their origin (not full source).
- KMS/HSM: primary keys are in a customer-dedicated KMS namespace; master keys are HSM-backed (AWS CloudHSM). Only a small set of ops engineers have split-key access; we'll provide roles and an excerpt of the key rotation policy.

I'll attach a draft CSV (attachment stub) for review before we send.

—Karthik

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <security@medsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor roster validation + evidence package (MedSecure request)

Hi Priyanka — thanks for your patience. Attached is a preliminary evidence package and shared Drive link: 

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessors_20250909.csv (authoritative roster; columns: vendor_name, primary_service, region, role, contract_start, data_scope)
- sbom_redwood_runtime_20250909.pdf (high-level runtime component list, SPDX header)
- sig-lite-response-20250910.docx (SIG-lite answers for infrastructure and data protection)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodMedSecure (read-only, expires 2025-12-31)
Public attestations: SOC 2 report (redacted) and ISO 27001 scope included in the Drive folder.

Summary of KMS/HSM posture:
- Master keys: HSM-backed (CloudHSM) in a customer-segmented namespace
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with mutual auth for internal services
- Key separation: customer data keys are generated per-customer; only the KMS service account plus approved ops roles can perform encrypt/decrypt operations; all key usage is logged to a tamper-evident audit stream.

We redacted internal account IDs and any pricing fields. If you need the unredacted outputs under an NDA/CDA, we can open a secure transfer channel.

Next steps: please confirm if the package meets your needs or if there's anything specific missing by EOD 2025-09-12.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

---

From: Priyanka Rao <security@medsecure.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSecure Compliance Team <compliance@medsecure.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor roster validation + evidence package (MedSecure request)

Mina — received the package, thank you. Quick follow-up items after an initial pass: 

1) Can you provide a short log sample or pointer to the tamper-evident audit stream for KMS key usage (we don't need full logs, but a time-windowed example showing key rotation and access decisions)?
2) The SBOM is helpful; can you confirm which runtime components are built from third-party source vs compiled vendor binaries (we flagged three kernel modules we saw in the PDF).
3) For the subcontractor roster, please add a column that indicates whether subprocessors are under EU data processing agreements (yes/no) — that will help our legal team.

If you can get these three items by next Tuesday (2025-09-16), we should be able to close the review. If any of those require an NDA or separate secure channel, flag that and we'll get it in motion.

Thanks — Priyanka

---

On Wed, 10 Sep 2025 at 10:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Priyanka — thanks for the review and the clear asks.
> 
> 1) We'll prepare a redacted KMS access sample (timestamped entries, user role, action) and host it on a secure S3 bucket with short-lived credentials.
> 2) I'll ask Engineering to annotate the SBOM to indicate third-party source vs vendor-provided binary.
> 3) We'll update the CSV to add the EU DPA column and resend.
> 
> If MedSecure's legal team prefers, we can also push the unredacted roster under a mutual NDA — we have a standard secure transfer process.
> 
> I'll aim to have the three updates by 2025-09-16.
> 
> Mina
> Head of Trust & Compliance
> mina.haddad@redwood.com
